exercises.q: Match each word with its meaning (Wiktionary's definitions).
exercises.why: From Wiktionary: говори́ть — to speak, to talk (perfective поговорить); разгово́р — talk, conversation; проговори́ть — to say, to utter; заговори́ть — to begin to speak.

**заговорил** — заговори́ть (perfective): to begin to speak; to talk someone's ear off (tire someone out by one's talk); to exorcise, to bewitch, to charm, to cast a spell, to enchant. Wiktionary: за- + говори́ть.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: I was the first to begin speaking.
exercises.why: **заговорил** — заговори́ть (perfective): to begin to speak; to talk someone's ear off (tire someone out by one's talk); to exorcise, to bewitch, to charm, to cast a spell, to enchant. Wiktionary: за- + говори́ть.

exercises.q: Your temper is quick, but the way you speak is terrible.
exercises.why: **говор** — го́вор: (colloquial) the sound of talking, the sound of voices, the sound of speech; murmur; dialect, patois, regionalism; pronunciation, accent.
exercises.context: One family: which of its words fits?

exercises.q: Tom's last name is hard to pronounce.
exercises.why: **выговорить** — вы́говорить (perfective): to articulate, to pronounce, to utter; (colloquial) to reserve for oneself, to stipulate, to set as a condition (in a contract, transaction, etc.); (colloquial) to censure, to reprimand, to rebuke. Wiktionary: вы́- + говори́ть.

exercises.q: This sentence is so hard to say.
exercises.why: **выговорить** — вы́говорить (perfective): to articulate, to pronounce, to utter; (colloquial) to reserve for oneself, to stipulate, to set as a condition (in a contract, transaction, etc.); (colloquial) to censure, to reprimand, to rebuke. Wiktionary: вы́- + говори́ть.
